items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I played with Kid Rene at the Cadillac nightclub.

ctx.x: I think it was before Depression. Because lots of times I played funeral with them and played parade. Then when they had dance at the background, I used to play with them in the brass band at the background. And Kid Rene was upstairs in a dance hall. She used to have two bands. Kid Rene would be upstairs and the brass band would be downstairs.
Were you playing dance band work at the same time?

items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: He'd play with me until he died. We worked at the Brown Derby on Canal Street.

ctx.x: Well, did anybody in the band, I mean, were any of those members that you mentioned, were they readers at all? Not that I know of.

Never used the arrangements then, never had the music there for any of those. They let him just play what they, what they thought went, did it sound good? And he had the biggest reputation around here, and then the trumpet player. And then another one had a big reputation around here, Kid René. Kid René had a bigger reputation than Louis Armstrong. Just say he didn't want to go away from him, he had the best opportunity of his life. They're begging him, come to Chicago. King Alba wanted to send him to him. He…
Well, uh, when you played on the trucks like everybody petite, uh, what kind of a drum set did you have at that time, alright?

items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: The interviewee denies going to Kid Renee's band and states he worked with Sidney Desweeney instead. No personal connection or interaction with Kid Renee is described.

ctx.x: But I tell you, I was tough in my days. I was plenty tough in my days. Anybody tell you about me. I was plenty tough. I was plenty tough. I was plenty tough. Which, I'm old now, but I don't worry about none of them. You get around all right. I don't worry about none of them. You're all right, yeah. Ain't a place I ever played if I can't go back and play or if they don't want me to come back and see about a job.
Yeah. Well after you left Buddy Petite, did you go right away to Kid Renee's band? No, no, no.
After I left Buddy Petite, I worked with Sidney Desweeney. I see. Yeah. I worked with Sidney Desweeney about two years.
